name: Leveraged/inverse ETF end-of-day rebalancing (last-30-minute momentum or reversal)
author_year: Barbon, Beckmeyer, Buraschi and Moerke (2021, SSRN 3925725; Swiss Finance Institute WP 2021/14). Related: Tuzun (2013, FEDS WP 2013-48, https://www.federalreserve.gov/pubs/feds/2013/201348/201348pap.pdf); Baltussen, Da and Soebhag (2026, end-of-day reversal, working paper).
instrument: Paper: single stocks and index constituents held by leveraged ETFs (equity options and LETF rebalancing). Maven MT5 mapping: US100/US500 index CFD only, as an index-level proxy. The stock-level effect cannot be traded directly on Maven [uncertain].
timeframe: Intraday: last 30 minutes of the US session (15:30-16:00 ET). Barbon uses the 15:30 price as the signal point; Baltussen uses ROD3 (close to 15:00) and LH (15:30-16:00).
entry_rule: Barbon et al.: LETF rebalancing demand is a function of the index move so far in the day. A 1% index move induces LETF buying (or selling) into the close. Price pressure in the last half hour can be momentum (same direction as the day's move) or reversal, depending on the sign and size of the aggregate gamma imbalance relative to average dollar volume. Exact rule for a 15:30 entry: [uncertain: no rule expressed as a tradeable index-level threshold found in the sources read]. Tuzun (2013): a 1% S&P 500 move produces LETF rebalancing that adds about 6.9 bp in the last hour for an average large-cap stock.
exit_rule: Exit at the 16:00 ET close (30-minute hold). Barbon et al. find roughly one-third of the LETF impact reverses at the next open, so a close exit captures the impact but overnight reversion is a risk (for a hold that crosses the close).
stop_rule: No stop defined in the sources. With a 30-minute hold, any stop is a discretionary choice [uncertain].
trades_per_year: Up to about 250 if traded daily. With a rebalancing-size threshold filter (only large-imbalance days), fewer [uncertain: threshold not defined on index level].
overnight_weekend: No, if the exit is at the 16:00 ET close. The next-open reversal in Barbon et al. is an overnight risk that a hold through the close would take.
signal_window_definition: Last half hour, 15:30-16:00 ET. Barbon: signal at 15:30 price; Baltussen: ROD3 (close t-1 to 15:00) and LH (15:30-16:00). DST: the window is in New York time; a Maven broker-time implementation must shift with US DST (two shifts per year) [uncertain: broker time offset not verified].
sample_period: Barbon et al.: optionable stocks May 2005 to July 2020; LETF data January 2012 to December 2019. Rolling three-year subsamples 2012-2019 are significant in all windows. Tuzun: 2011-2012 data. Baltussen et al. (2026): stock-level TAQ data since 1993, 5-year rolling panels, reversal present in almost every window. No 2023+ sample found.
out_of_sample: No formal out-of-sample trading test in the sources read. Barbon et al. use rolling three-year subsamples (in-sample, sub-periods). Baltussen et al. use 5-year rolling panels. No 2020+ or 2023+ out-of-sample result [uncertain].
cost_assumption: Barbon et al.: not clearly stated in the sections read. Baltussen et al.: gross long-short reversal of 3.55 bp per day (value-weighted) and 5.81 bp per day (equal-weighted); the authors say the strategy may not be exploitable after transaction costs for most investors. Maven cost not measured [uncertain].
reported_metrics: Barbon et al.: long-short strategy annualized Sharpe about 3 (5 in a second specification), success rate 58.13% (61.91%), alpha unexplained by standard risk factors. LETF rebalancing effect: 430% of average last-half-hour return per one standard deviation of flow in one version, 403% in another (version conflict). Baltussen et al. (2026): long-short 3.55 bp per day (8.9% per year, value-weighted) and 5.81 bp per day (14.6% per year, equal-weighted), t-statistics above 10 in portfolio sorts. Tuzun (2013): +6.9 bp price and +22.7 bp daily volatility in an average large-cap stock per 1% S&P 500 move.
third_party_replication: Partial. Baltussen, Da and Soebhag (Erasmus / Notre Dame) is a separate team that finds the stock-level last-half-hour reversal and says gamma and LETF hedging explain only part of it. A 2024 survey (Quantitative Finance and Economics, doi 10.3934/QFE.2024031) concludes that most papers have serious methodological errors and that economic associations look insignificant. A Journal of Empirical Finance-style study (ScienceDirect, HTTP 403, read from search snippet only) finds statistically significant but economically insignificant effects [uncertain].
evidence_grade: Working papers (Barbon et al. 2021 SSRN and FSI WP; Baltussen et al. 2026; Tuzun FEDS staff WP 2013-48). Peer-reviewed: 2024 survey in Quantitative Finance and Economics; the JEF-style study (snippet only, unverified).
decay_status: Conflicting. Barbon et al. working paper text: the LETF impact 'remained constant' across 2012-2019 rolling subsamples, while the delta-hedging impact increased. A search-snippet version of the same paper states LETF effects 'have decreased over time' and are shorter-lived. The 2024 survey says the economic associations look insignificant. No 2023-2026 decay test found [uncertain].
regime_split: Barbon et al.: significant in every rolling three-year subsample 2012-2019. Tuzun: impact especially large in 2009 and the 2011 European sovereign crisis (high-volatility regimes). Baltussen et al.: reversal persistent across 5-year windows. No pre/post-2022 split found [uncertain].
data_source_requirement: Intraday stock trades (TAQ), LETF AUM and holdings (ETFGlobal), equity option open interest and volume (OptionMetrics, exchange data). None of this is on Maven. A Maven-only version needs US100/US500 intraday prices and an index-level LETF proxy (AUM and leverage not available) [uncertain: LETF flow data source not identified].
min_lot_fit_5k10k: 0.01 US100 = $0.10 per point. Index-level effect is small (Tuzun: a few bp in large caps per 1% move). A hypothetical 50-point stop on a 30-minute NQ trade = $5 risk on 0.01 lot = 0.1% of a 5K account and 0.05% of a 10K account [uncertain: 30-minute NQ range and stop not measured].
fn_rule_fit: Single 30-minute position per day, no grid, no tick-scalp pattern: no HFT concern. The 15:30-16:00 ET window is not normally a high-impact release slot, but FOMC (14:00 ET) and some data releases must be checked against the +-5 minute rule [uncertain]. Open-risk within 3% at 0.01 lot.
bot_policy_compliance: Yes in principle: an EA can compute the index move at 15:30 ET and execute once; no messaging dependency. The broker time conversion is a technical requirement.
event_overlap: Exact overlap with the US closing auction (MOC imbalance publication about 15:50 ET), option expiration Fridays (close), quarterly index rebalancing (third Friday of March, June, September, December), and FOMC (14:00 ET) on scheduled days.
overlap_with_existing: Possible overlap with SWEEP_CORE if Sweep entries fall in the last 30 minutes of the US session; the Sweep timing was not checked against this window [uncertain].
rejected_catalog_hit: Two direct vetoes. (1) baltussen_last30_momentum (REJECTED, 2026-11-17): on NQ n=3639, gross +0.75 bp, measured cost -1.46 bp per trade, annual -3.7%, 2022+ gross -0.39 bp; XAU similar. This is the same last-30-minute momentum rule family, so the cost-measured test already eliminates the simple index version. (2) gao_itsm_first30_last30 (REJECTED): first-30 to last-30 momentum on 8 markets, all cost-negative. 'elenenler --kontrol leveraged' returned no entry.
base_rate_check: Yes. The unconditional last-30-minute drift must be subtracted before attributing a move to rebalancing. Sign is conditional on the imbalance and liquidity, so an unconditioned test has no base-rate edge. Baltussen et al. (2026) report the reversal among stocks as a base-rate-type pattern, which conflicts with the momentum reading [uncertain].
pitfall_risk: Sign ambiguity (momentum vs reversal depends on the imbalance measure; the same family is reported with opposite signs across papers). Post-hoc sign selection risk. Stock-level evidence does not map to index CFD. Gross effect of 3-6 bp per day sits near the CFD spread, and the catalog's momentum veto already shows cost loss. Decay evidence and unmeasured LETF flow data. Small sample of tradeable days in any Maven-only test.
